contrast_tests.primary: the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval on the difference of means; the paper states a difference in accuracy points, and that is the quantity this interval is an interval for
contrast_tests.secondary: a two-sided Mann-Whitney U test at alpha = 0.05, which tests stochastic dominance rather than a difference of means
contrast_tests.why_they_can_disagree: The returned accuracy is bounded above by the grid optimum and is strongly left-skewed. A shift of the mean carried by a thin left tail can leave the two distributions interleaved, so the interval excludes zero where U does not; a consistent shift of the bulk that is small in points can do the reverse. The two are reported together and every cell where they part is listed here.

evolution.decided_by: the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval on the difference of means

local.decided_by: the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval on the difference of means

random.decided_by: the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval on the difference of means

protocol.cost_model: sum over the queried cells of the benchmark's own recorded train_times (mean seconds per epoch) x epochs (200) / 3600, in GPU-hours; the search field supplies the cost, since that is the training run the search performs. This is NAS-Bench-201's record of its authors' training cost, not a measurement of ours.
protocol.evolution_mutation: one uniformly chosen edge set to one of the four other operations, uniformly; age-based (oldest) removal
protocol.local_search: uniform random start, best-improvement over the 24 single-edge neighbours, random restart at a local optimum; every neighbour inspected is a query
protocol.query: one distinct architecture trained; re-visiting an architecture the run has already trained is free and does not consume budget
protocol.random_search: uniform random sample of N distinct cells
protocol.recalibration: scipy.stats.rankdata of the labels inside the fitted sample
protocol.ridge: degree-2 ridge of s35_nb201.fit (= surrogate.PairwiseRidge): 6 edge main effects + all 15 edge-pair interactions
protocol.seed_scheme: numpy default_rng([2026, dataset_index, algorithm_index, seed, budget]); budget is 0 for every algorithm but the recipe, whose random sample depends on N
protocol.training: none: every evaluation is a lookup in data/nb201_all.pickle

protocol_bias.what: the same replay with the search signal set to the reported test column instead of the validation column, which is the protocol the redistributed table forces on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet16-120

protocol_note: The redistributed table exposes a single accuracy field (eval_acc1es) per dataset key. CIFAR-10 therefore follows the standard protocol -- the algorithms see only cifar10-valid (train-split model, validation-split accuracy) and the reported number is the cifar10 final test accuracy, which no algorithm reads -- while for CIFAR-100 and ImageNet16-120 no separate validation column exists, so the search signal and the reported accuracy are necessarily the same field. The CIFAR-100 and ImageNet16-120 columns are therefore optimistic by whatever a validation/test split would cost. That cost is not left as an assertion: CIFAR-10 carries both columns, so the same replay is run there under both protocols and the difference is reported in protocol_bias, together with the spread of that difference across the four algorithms, which is the only part of it that could reorder the table.
